page: Microsoft Azure F64amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, alongside a substantial 7559 GB of local storage. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which accelerate vector and neural network operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the F64amds_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests. Its memory subsystem achieves a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 11,893.77 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 193.26 GB/sec. Database and memory operations are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations reaching 170.17 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring in the top decile. The system also exhibits strong performance in low-parameter LLM inference, processing 135M model prompts at 5,641.46 tokens per second.

Given its high resource density, featuring 512 GB of RAM and over 7.5 TB of local storage, the F64amds_v7 offers a highly qualitative cost-to-performance ratio for memory-heavy and storage-bound workloads. The absence of a dedicated GPU makes it less suitable for large-scale deep learning training, but its high clock speed and massive memory capacity make it ideal for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, high-throughput static web serving, and intensive data analytics pipelines.
